approach: Root cause: a file kept by hand as a mirror of a governing source (xtask/shard-timings.txt, docs/decisions.md, status::BUILD_PATHS against the CI athena-bin key, docs/ontology.toml) is tested for its shape only, or checked late, so content that contradicts the source passes until the final verdict. Fix at the origin with one registry, crates/athena-core/src/mirrors.rs: each entry names a mirror file, its source and a comparison rule, and pure rule functions compare content. Four rules: (a) shard-timings `--test` and `--lib` lines equal the units on disk; (b) docs/decisions.md starts with the exact bytes of its base version; (c) the CI athena-bin hashFiles globs and the BUILD_PATHS list in the mirror file crates/athena-core/src/status.rs cover each other both ways (this finds a real drift today, so BUILD_PATHS gains four roots); (d) docs/ontology.toml terms against the governing docs, through one shared walk that moves from the ontology test into mirrors.rs. Revision changes: rule (c) now parses BUILD_PATHS out of the status.rs it checks (the compiled constant of the installed binary is never used as rule data), and the producer loop charges a producer only with drift on a mirror or source its own change set touches, so drift already present at the base is never sent back. The before-handover call site stays the producer loop's self-check in run/producer.rs, which runs after every producer report and before verification. A repo-level athena-cli test target runs the registry over the real files (all entries, no touch filter) and over a drifted fixture per entry, so a new entry is covered with no other edit. checks.rs stays unchanged (see decision 9).

decisions.choice: One registry REGISTRY: &[Mirror] with Mirror { name, mirror, source: Source, rule: Rule }. Source is Path | Globs | GitHead | Docs; Rule is TimingUnits | AppendOnly | HashFilesCover | OntologyTerms (no rule carries data copied from the running binary). check_entry(entry, root, base) wraps every inner finding in a Drift { mirror, message }. check_all(root, base, touched: Option<&[String]>) runs every entry whose mirror file exists; with Some(paths) it runs only entries whose mirror or source the paths touch (Mirror::watches). is_athena_source(root) (setup.sh, xtask/shard-timings.txt and crates/athena-core/Cargo.toml all exist) gates the producer-loop use.
decisions.reason: The cause is that nothing makes a mirror declare how it is compared to its source. A registry makes the declaration the unit and the repo test iterates it. The gate keeps jobs on other repositories, which may have their own docs/decisions.md, from being forced to append-only. The touch filter (critic finding 10, last sentence) means a producer is charged only with drift on files it changed or whose source it changed, never with drift already in the base.

rejected.option: One more one-off test per mirror, as the five jobs did
rejected.why: Fixes one instance and leaves the class.

rejected.option: Put the registry in xtask
rejected.why: xtask does not depend on athena-core, so it cannot reach the other mirrors' code, and xtask tests run in a heavy shard outside the producer loop.

rejected.why: docs/decisions.md append-only is Athena's own convention, so other repositories would get false send-backs.

rejected.option: Charge all drift found in the snapshot to the producer
rejected.why: A mirror already drifting at the base would be sent back although the producer cannot have caused it.

decisions.choice: Rule (c) reads BUILD_PATHS from the mirror file it names: status_build_paths(status_rs_text) finds `pub const BUILD_PATHS`, starts after the `=` (so the `[&str; 9]` type is skipped), reads to the next `;` and collects the quoted strings. hash_glob_problems(ci_text, roots) takes those roots. Mirror = crates/athena-core/src/status.rs, Source::Path(.github/workflows/ci.yml). (i) Each hashFiles glob on an `athena-bin-` key line must be covered by a root (a root ending `/` covers a glob starting with it, a file root its exact name); else the message says add the path to BUILD_PATHS in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs. (ii) Each root must be covered by a glob (a dir root needs a glob that starts with it and ends `**`); else it says add the glob to every athena-bin key. A ci.yml with no such key line, or a status.rs whose array cannot be parsed, is a drift. The athena-cli repo test asserts the parsed list equals the compiled status::BUILD_PATHS, so the parse cannot silently diverge. BUILD_PATHS becomes nine roots: crates/, xtask/, rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, athena.toml, defaults.toml, setup.sh, docs/system-facts.md; stale_build_line prints the list from the constant.
decisions.reason: Critic finding 10: the first design compared the snapshot's ci.yml to the constant compiled into the installed binary, which can be older than the tree. A producer who correctly edited both would be sent back, one who edited only status.rs would be missed, and an old install would send back every job. Parsing the snapshot's own status.rs makes the rule judge the files in the work tree. The drift is real: xtask/tests/policy.rs (lines 783, 897-1000) forces the key to equal xtask BUILD_INPUT_GLOBS (xtask/src/main.rs 267-277), the true input set; athena.toml is compiled in (athena-gate lib.rs 33 BUILTIN_CONFIG), docs/system-facts.md too (athena-context briefs.rs 1671 SYSTEM_FACTS) and rust-toolchain.toml changes the compiler, yet touches_build (status.rs 23-29) and stale_build_line (35-58) ignore them, so a landing that changes them leaves a stale binary with no rebuild. defaults.toml is an xtask build input; adding it costs at most an extra rebuild and keeps one rule with no excusal list.

rejected.why: Judges the work tree by the binary's older build; false and missed send-backs.

decisions.choice: Rule (d) shares the whole walk with the ontology test. mirrors.rs gets plain-data types OntologyTerm { name, aliases, sources, senses, excused } and pub fns is_word_char, phrase_in, names_term, is_identifying, Hit, scan, is_decision_id, names_of, scanned_files, term_hits, excuse_ok, uncovered_lines, parse_ontology(toml_text) (toml_edit, which athena-core already depends on) and ontology_problems(toml_text, read_file). The inner uncovered-line text from the loop at crates/athena-cli/tests/ontology.rs 413-430 ('{name}: {path}:{n} names the term as a definition or role and no sense or excuse covers it: {line}') is unchanged. check_entry wraps it in a Drift whose message starts with `docs/ontology.toml:` and ends with the fix `add a senses entry or an excuse for that term in docs/ontology.toml`. Tests assert the wrapped text. The ontology test keeps its serde types and its sense/says and excuse-shape checks, converts each serde Term with plain() and calls the shared fns; a new test both_parsers_read_the_same_terms asserts plain(serde term) == parse_ontology(text) on the real file.
decisions.reason: Moving only the line matchers left a second term walk in mirrors.rs. athena-core has toml_edit but not toml, so the parser cannot be shared; the remaining difference is the parse, which the agreement test guards. Critic finding 13: the inner message names neither the mirror nor a fix, so the Drift wrapper supplies both and the inner text stays unchanged.

decisions.choice: Rule (a) derives `--test` and `--lib` units from disk: crates/*/tests/*.rs, crates/*/tests/*/main.rs and xtask/tests (unit `<dir name> --test <stem>`), and crates/*/src/lib.rs (unit `<dir name> --lib`). missing_timing_lines(units, timings_text) reports a unit missing from the file and a `--test` or `--lib` line with no unit; `--doc` and `--bin` lines are never reported. The entry's Source::Globs lists those patterns and a small segment-wise glob matcher backs Mirror::watches. A real-repo test derived_units_agree_with_cargo_metadata runs `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 --locked` (as xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs does around line 120) and asserts the `--test` and `--lib` units of targets with test=true equal the derived set. D158 says `--doc` and `--bin` stay with the heavier oracle in ci_shards.rs (around line 420).
decisions.reason: A new crate's lib is as likely to be missed as a test file, and both are cheap facts on disk. The agreement test compares the derived copy with cargo's own answer on the real repo. `--bin` names can be renamed (athena-cli's bin is `athena`) and `--doc` depends on the doctest flag, so deriving them would be a guess; the limit is stated.

decisions.choice: Rule (b) append_only_problem(base: &[u8], new: &[u8]) fails unless base is a byte prefix of new, and names docs/decisions.md, the first changed line and the fix (append, do not edit). The base comes from an injected closure `&dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`. The producer loop builds it only when `snapshot.base()` is Some(base) (it returns Option<&str>, crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs line 131): `move |p| snapshot.git().show_file(base, p).ok().flatten()`; when base() is None the closure returns None for every path, which skips rule (b). Git::show_file (athena-git lib.rs 453) takes &str and returns Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>. The repo test uses git_base(root) with HEAD. A None base skips the rule. crates/athena-cli/src/decisions.rs keeps its PINNED_LEN/PINNED_SHA256 test for committed history.
decisions.reason: This is the rag3 prevention. The producer's snapshot is a git repository whose base commit is the dispatch base, so the base text is available while it edits. Critic finding 14: base() is optional, so the call is guarded.

decisions.choice: The before-handover call site is the producer loop's existing self-check in crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs (after unmet/unchanged/gate/outside, lines 285-320). Add `let mirrors = if self.nested.is_none() && !changes.is_empty() { mirror_drift_in(&snapshot, &changed) } else { Vec::new() };` after the gate (line 306), add `&& mirrors.is_empty()` to the break condition (lines 313-318), push `files kept by hand disagree with their source: ...` into `problems` after the `report_problems` clone (line 343, as the gate does, so the verifier is not told the report lacked it), print a ui line when a drift remains at the limit (near line 385) and break as the gate does. Apply `append_mirror_drift(text, &mirrors)` to the result of the `attempt_brief = match` (lines 407-423). In run/send_back.rs append_mirror_drift returns the text unchanged for an empty list; otherwise it puts one leading sentence before the text (as the scope, gate and replay builders do in send_back_text_scoped, lines 134-171): 'Files that are kept by hand disagree with the source they summarize; this is a reason for this send-back whether or not criteria are listed.' It then appends a section listing each Drift message, which names the file and the fix. mirror_drift_in returns an empty list unless mirrors::is_athena_source(snapshot.dir()), and calls check_all(dir, base, Some(&changed)). It shares the single PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS slot (line 374). A nested run is judged by the outer job.
decisions.reason: The mechanism the 'mechanism' default and criterion 5 ask for is an invocation, not a sentence. The loop runs before verification on the one-commit snapshot, so the base is readable. Critic finding 12: with drift alone the match falls to send_back_text, whose intro speaks only of unmet criteria, so the wrapper adds the leading sentence and the loop test asserts it.

risks.risk: Changing BUILD_PATHS makes a landing that touches athena.toml, defaults.toml, rust-toolchain.toml or docs/system-facts.md trigger a rebuild in the drain, and a drain test that landed athena.toml (tests/drain.rs line 3117) may assert no rebuild.

risks.risk: The loop hook sends back on a false positive, for example drift already in the base.
risks.mitigation: The touch filter charges only drift on mirrors or sources the producer changed; the real-repo test runs at base in step 5 and any drift there is fixed or the rule corrected first; the loop sends back once, then leaves with a ui line, and the configured `cargo test --locked` is the backstop.

risks.risk: The touch filter is too narrow (a producer changes a source in a way Mirror::watches misses) so drift passes the loop.
risks.mitigation: The loop is the early signal only; the same registry runs unfiltered in athena-cli --test mirrors under the configured test check, so the drift is caught at verification. Unit tests cover watches for each Source form.

risks.risk: The registry runs on a repository that is not Athena's source and fails it.
risks.mitigation: is_athena_source gate, plus skip when a mirror file is absent; a loop test uses a repository without those files and asserts no send-back.

risks.risk: Moving the ontology walk changes ontology test behavior, or the two parsers diverge.
risks.mitigation: Functions move verbatim with messages unchanged; the existing ontology tests run; both_parsers_read_the_same_terms compares plain data of both parsers on the real file.

risks.risk: Derived `--test` and `--lib` units diverge from cargo's target set, for example a [[test]] with a custom path.
risks.mitigation: derived_units_agree_with_cargo_metadata on the real repo; on disagreement the producer fixes the derivation, not the timings file.

risks.risk: The narrow parse of BUILD_PATHS breaks if status.rs is reformatted.
risks.mitigation: Parse failure is itself a drift with a message, and the repo test asserts parsed == compiled constant.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in mirrors::tests and loop tests in run::tests (names beginning `mirrors_`). Pure tests call the rule functions with literal text, each with a failing and a passing case. missing_timing_lines: a test file absent from the timings fails and the message names xtask/shard-timings.txt and the line to add; a stale `--test` line fails; a `--doc`, `--bin` or other-package line is not reported. append_only_problem: a rewritten decision line fails and names docs/decisions.md and the first changed line; added text passes. hash_glob_problems with roots from status_build_paths on a literal status.rs text: a ci key hashing `athena.toml` while the roots lack it fails with `add ... to BUILD_PATHS in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs`; a root missing from the key fails with `add the glob`; a dir root with only `crates/` and no `**` fails; no athena-bin key fails; an unparsable array fails; a matching pair passes. uncovered_lines and check_entry for ontology: a governing-doc line `Hermes: a role ...` for a term with only a tool sense yields a Drift whose message starts with `docs/ontology.toml:`, contains the unchanged inner text and ends with `add a senses entry or an excuse`; a covering sense or a valid excuse passes. check_all over a tempfile tree with a fixed base closure: the clean tree gives none; a None base skips rule (b); a tree that is not an Athena source gives none via is_athena_source; with touched=Some(&["README.md"]) a drift already in the tree (test file missing from timings) is not reported, and with touched=Some(&["crates/demo/tests/b.rs"]) it is; a tree whose status.rs and ci.yml were both edited consistently (tree constant differs from the compiled one) gives none, and one with only status.rs edited gives a Drift. Loop tests in run::tests with the fake-agent harness: the producer adds crates/demo/tests/b.rs and no timings line, so the second producer prompt carries `## Sent back`, the leading sentence, `xtask/shard-timings.txt` and the fix, and the job is sent back once; a producer script `fixing_timings_on_send_back`, modelled on reconciling_on_send_back (run/tests.rs line 2288), adds the timings line only when its prompt contains '## Sent back' and then reaches the verifier; a clean producer is not sent back; a drift committed in the base and untouched by the producer is not sent back; a repository that is not Athena's source is not sent back.
demonstrations.observes: All tests pass. Each negative case returns a non-empty Vec whose text names the offending file and the fix. The fixed-on-send-back loop test counts producer runs 2 and verifier runs 1; the clean, untouched-drift and non-Athena cases count producer runs 1 with no `## Sent back` in any prompt.
